Palladium(0)-Catalyzed Regioselective Synthesis of Macrocycles
from Allenes with a Nucleophilic Functionality and Organic
Iodides
Xin Huang, a Xinpeng Jiang, a Chunling Fu, a and Shengming Ma a,*
a Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310027,
Zhejiang, People/C29s Republic of China
Fax : (
+ 86)-21-6260-9305; e-mail: masm@sioc.ac.cn
Received: July 6, 2013; Revised: August 22, 2013; Published online: November 11, 2013
Supporting information for this article is available on the WWW under http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/adsc.201300602.
Abstract: A highly regioselective synthesis of 15–
20-membered macrocycles via Pd(0)-catalyzed cou-
pling cyclization of allenes bearing a carbon or ni-
trogen nucleophilic functionality and organic io-
dides is reported. After oxidative addition and car-
bopalladation, anti-p-allyl palladium intermediates
were formed, which was followed by the exclusive
intramolecular nucleophilic attack at the terminal
carbon atom of the allene moiety to afford products
with yields ranging from 44–92% and E/Z ratios of
up to 97/3.
Keywords: allenes; carbopalladation; cyclization;
macrocycles
Macrocycles exist widely in natural products with re-
markable biological activities.
[1] The most commonly
used approaches to construct macrocycles include
ring-closing metathesis,
[2] macrolactonization,[3] mac-
rolactamization,[4] and multi-component macrocycliza-
tion.[5] In spite of all these developed methods, facile
and efficient new methods are still strongly in need.
Nowadays, allenes have been playing a more and
more important role in organic synthesis due to their
interesting chemical properties associated with the
two cumulated double bonds.
[6] T ransition metal-cata-
lyzed cyclization reactions of functionalized allenes in
the presence of organic halides have become very
useful methodologies to construct cyclic compounds.
[7]
However, there are only rare reports concerning the
synthesis of macrocycles via allenes.[8] It was noted
that the high dilution technique was applied to in-
crease the yields of macrocycles in both cases. In our
previous work, we have reported highly regio- and
stereoselective syntheses of 9- to 12-membered cyclic
compounds from the Pd(0)-catalyzed cyclization of al-
lenes having various carbon and nitrogen nucleophilic
functionalities.
[9] In this paper, we wish to report our
recent observation on the construction of 15- to 20-
membered macrocycles with high regioselectivity in
normal concentrations.
Initially, we conducted the reaction of 1a with PhI
under the catalysis of Pd ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh
3)4 (5 mol%) with
K2CO3 (4 equiv.) in DMA, 80 8C.[9] Fortunately, after
12 h, the reaction succeeded to afford the expected
product ( E)-3aa in 82% yield with a decent E/Z ratio
(95/5) (entry 1, Table 1). The structure of ( E)-3aa es-
pecially the C =C bond on the ring was further estab-
lished by an X-ray diffraction study (Figure 1).
[10]
Then these standard conditions were applied to inves-
tigate the reaction of 1a with other different organic
iodides (Table 1). Not only electron-rich (entries 2
and 3, T able 1) but also electron-deficient substituents
(entries 4–10, Table 1) could all be introduced into
aryl iodides: the corresponding 15-membered rings
were isolated in moderate to good yields (66–80%)
with high E/Z ratios (94/6–97/3). Interestingly, when
4-iodonitrobenzene ( 2k) was used, the corresponding
products ( E)-3ak and ( Z)-3ak were afforded in 79%
and 7% yields, respectively (entry 11, Table 1). 2-
Thienyl iodide ( 2l) could also react with 1a, which af-
forded ( E)-3al in 62% yield and ( Z)-3al in 7 % yield
(entry 13, Table 1). In addition, 1-( E)-hexenyl iodide
(2m) may also be applied, resulting in an isolated
yield of 35% for ( E)-3am and 25 % for ( Z)-3am, re-
spectively (entry 14, T able 1). We also investigated
the reaction of 1k on a 1-g scale under the optimized
conditions and obtained an 80% isolated yield of ( E)-
3ak and a 4% yield of ( Z)-3ak (entry 12, Table 1).
T o our surprise, when we tried the reaction of 1a
with 4-iodoanisole ( 2n), in addition to the expected
macrocycles ( E)-3an in 57% yield and ( Z)-3an in 3%
yield (by
1H NMR), a 9% yield of the phenyl-substi-
tuted product ( E)-3aa was also isolated [Eq. (1)]. The
possible mechanism of the formation of ( E)-3aa is

shown in Scheme 1. The oxidative addition of
PdACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh3)2 with 2n generates the 4-methoxyphenylpal-
ladium iodide intermediate IN-1. Then the reductive
elimination between PPh 3 and the 4-methoxyphenyl
group in intermediate IN-1 generates phosphonium
iodide IN-2, which undergoes the oxidative addition
with Pd ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh3)2 to generate a new intermediate IN-3,
causing the cleavage of the P /C0Ph bond. [11] Subsequent
reaction with 1a afforded the unexpected phenyl-sub-
stituted ( E)-3aa.
T o our delight, when a nitrogen nucleophile was in-
troduced, i.e., 1b, the expected azamacrocycle ( Z)-
3ba may also be obtained in 80% yield with a Z/E
ratio of 96/4. Interestingly, the reaction of 1c gave the
corresponding nitrogen-tethered heteromacrocycle
(E)-3ca in 44% yield as the only product. Similarly,
an oxygen tether may also be applied: the reaction of
1d afforded 39% isolated yield of ( E)-3da and 8%
isolated yield of ( Z)-3da (Scheme 2).
Subsequently, we conducted the reaction of 1e con-
taining only one C 6H4 unit with PhI under the previ-
ous standard conditions. Unfortunately, after 24 h, the
reaction afforded only 20% yield of macrocycle 3ea
with 38% recovery of 1e probably due to the in-
creased flexibility of the carbon chain in 1e (entry 1,
Table 2). Replacing Pd ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh3)4 (5 mol%) with
Pd2ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(dba)3
.CHCl3 (2.5 mol%) and TFP [10 mol%,
TFP = trisACHTUNGTRENNUNG(2-furyl)phosphine], the reaction afforded
25% yield of macrocycle 3ea albeit with 28% recov-
ery of 1e after 24 h (entry 2, T able 2). Interestingly,
with this catalytic system, after screening a series of
bases, we found that the reaction using K
3PO4 afford-
ed an 85% yield of macrocycle 3ea with an E/Z selec-
tivity of 85/15 (entries 3–5, T able 2). The reaction in
THF or CH
3CN afforded 3ea in much lower yields
(entries 6 and 7, Table 2).
Thus, the following conditions [Pd 2ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(dba)3
.CHCl3
(2.5 mol%), TFP (10 mol%), and K 3PO4 (4.0 equiv.)
in DMA, 80 8C] were established as the optimized
conditions for further study with the typical results
summarized in Table 3. The following issues should
be noted: (i) yields of macrocycles 3 range from 51%
to 92%; (ii) all the corresponding products were in-
separable E/Z mixtures except 3aa, and the E/Z
ratios range from 60/40 to 95/5; (iii) decreasing the ri-
gidity or increasing the size of the carbon chain in the
substrates may cause a decrease of the E/Z ratio.
Then we conducted the hydrogenation of products
3 under the conditions of Pd/C (10 mol%) and H
2
(30 bar) at room temperature. Interestingly, we found
that the solvent played an important role. For 3aa,
3ea, and 3ga, EtOAc/MeOH (1/1) was the proper
mixed solvent (entries 1, 2, 4, T able 3), but it did not
work for 3fa. Pleasantly, 3fa could be completely hy-
drogenated when CH 2Cl2/MeOH (1/1) was used in-
stead of EtOAc/MeOH (1/1) (entry 3, T able 3).

Unfortunately, neither of the mentioned mixed sol-
vents was effective for the hydrogenation of 3ha (en-
tries 1 and 2, Table 4). Then we tried to add CH 2Cl2
(0.1 mL) to EtOAc/MeOH (2.0 mL/2.0 mL) with
~ 95% of 3ha being recovered (entry 3, T able 4);
Luckily, when only 0.5 equiv. of CH
2Cl2 was added,
5% of 3ha was recovered after 58 h (entry 4, Table 4);
Replacing CH 2Cl2 (0.5 equiv.) with CHCl 3 (0.5 equiv.),
the complete hydrogenation of 3ha succeeded
(entry 5, Table 4). Increasing the amount of CHCl 3 to
1.0 equiv. could shorten the reaction time to 48 h
(entry 6, T able 4).
Subsequently, we found that this mixed solvent
[CHCl
3 (1.0 equiv) and EtOAc/MeOH (1/1)] was also
suitable for 3ia and 3ja (entries 6 and 7, Table 3) and
the amount of CHCl 3 should be increased to
2.0 equiv. for 3ka (entry 8, Table 3).
In addition, the substrate 1l with a Z C=C bond
could also react with PhI to afford a 69% isolated
yield of ( E)-3la and a 5% isolated yield of ( Z)-3la by
chromatography on silica gel with a purity of only
~ 86% [Eq. (2)].
In conclusion, we have developed an efficient
method for the synthesis of 15- to 20-membered mac-
rocycles via Pd(0)-catalyzed coupling–cyclization re-
action of functionalized allenes with organic iodides
in high regioselectivity without applying a high dilu-
tion technique. The rigidity and size of the carbon
chain in the substrates have a great influence on the
stereoselectivity of the formed macrocycles. The re-

gioselectivity may be rationalized by the presence of
an R group in the to-be-formed allylic Pd moiety, [12]
which is in its anti-form to avoid the steric repulsion
between the R group and the carbon chain bearing
the nucleophilic moiety (Scheme 3).
[13] Further studies
in this area are being pursued in our laboratory.
Experimental Section
General Experimental Methods
1H and 13C nuclear magnetic resonance spectra were record-
ed on an instrument operated at 300 MHz for 1H and
75 MHz for 13C. Deuterochloroform (CDCl 3) was used as
solvent in all NMR experiments. Chemical shifts ( d) are
given in parts per million (ppm). Infrared spectra were re-
corded from films of pure samples on sodium chloride
plates for liquids or in the form of KBr discs for the solid
samples. Mass and HR-mass spectra were carried out in the
ESI mode. Thin layer chromatography was performed on
pre-coated glassback plates and visualized with UV light at
254 nm. Flash column chromatography was performed on
silica gel. THF was refluxed in the presence of sodium wire
using diphenyl ketone as indicator and distilled right before
use. DMA used was stirred with CaH
2 for 12 h at 80 8C and
distilled under vacuum before use. K 2CO3 was bought from
Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd. Pd 2ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(dba)3
.CHCl3,
Pd/C and K 3PO4 were bought from Alfa Aesar. TFP was
bought from Aldrich.
General Procedure for Pd(0)-Catalyzed Coupling–
Cyclization of 1a with Different Organic Iodides 2
under Standard Conditions
Preparation of ( E)-3aa; Typical Procedure I
To a flame-dried Schlenk tube containing K 2CO3
(109.8 mg, 0.8 mmol) were added Pd ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh3)4 (12.0 mg,
0.01 mmol), 2a (81.7 mg, 0.4 mmol), DMA (0.5 mL), a solu-
tion of 1a (w/w = 9.54% in DMA) (1.3637 g, 0.2 mmol), and
DMA (1.2 mL) sequentially under a nitrogen atmosphere.
The reaction was complete after being stirred at 80
8C for
12 h as monitored by TLC (eluent: petroleum ether/ethyl
acetate/dichloromethane = 5/1/1). The resulting mixture was
quenched with 10 mL of H
2O, extracted with ether (30 mL /C148
3), washed with water and brine, and dried over anhydrous
Na
2SO4. After filtration and evaporation of the solvent, the
E/Z ratio (95/5) was determined by 1H NMR analysis of the
crude product with CH 2Br2 as the internal standard. Chro-
matography on silica gel [eluent: dichloromethane/ethyl ace-
tate (40/1)] afforded ( E)-3aa as a white solid; yield:
119.7 mg (82%); mp 215–216 8C( n-hexane/DCM); 1H NMR

Preparation of 4ea; Typical Procedure II

atmosphere. The reaction was complete after being stirred
at 80
8C for 12 h as monitored by TLC (eluent: petroleum

temperature for 48 h, and the resulting mixture was filtered
through a short pad of silica gel eluted with 30 mL of ethyl
